1.why: All MFA endpoints load the session via getSession and only operate on mfa(s.accountId), with no client-supplied account identifier.

2.why: Identity challenges bind code, identityKey, and accountId, and OTP/recovery checks use the session account’s own secret/codes, so one user’s code does not authenticate another.

3.why: Enabling MFA in verify-otp updates only that account’s Mfa record and does not invalidate or revoke any other existing sessions in the sessions map.

4.why: The OTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encrypt/decrypt) and backup codes are stored as PBKDF2 hashes via protect(), not plaintext.

5.why: tokens, digits, base32 secrets, recovery codes, and keys are all produced with crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: Session and challenge cookies are HttpOnly; there is no localStorage/sessionStorage use for secrets, OTPs, or session tokens.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP, and recovery input with emailOK/phoneOK/otpOK/recoveryInput before use.

8.why: Dynamic values are applied with textContent/JSON responses and a nonce-based CSP, not unescaped HTML interpolation of user input.

9.why: Sign-in accepts redirect only when it is in the ROUTES allow-list (signin/setup/verify/backup/confirmed/settings); no open external redirects.

10.why: secureHeaders sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: sessionCookie and challengeCookie set HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict (with __Host- prefix).

12.why: The client explicitly log()s manual setup secrets and backup recovery codes into the on-page Logs panel and console, so they are not kept out of logs.

13.why: Identity challenges are single-use with CHALLENGE_MS expiry; provisioning is time-bound; TOTP acceptance is window-bound; backup codes are marked used after success.

14.why: identityAttempts, otpAttempts, and recoveryAttempts lock out after MAX_FAILURES (5) for LOCK_MS (10 minutes).

15.why: Sign-in issues a new session id and deletes the prior cookie session; getSession enforces idle/absolute timeouts; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
